summary: Luigi's Mansion was supposed to be a prize—a mansion Luigi had won in a contest he did not remember entering, which should have been the first warning sign. When Luigi arrived to explore his new property, he found Mario missing, a haunted estate full of hostile ghosts, and a situation that only he could resolve. For the first time in his life, Luigi could not rely on Mario. For the first time, he had to be the hero. He succeeded. He defeated King Boo, rescued Mario, and proved that he possessed capabilities that his anxiety normally concealed. And then, when the adventure ended, the narrative compressed his achievement into a footnote of Mario's broader legend. 'Mario was rescued by his brother'—passive voice, emphasizing the rescue target rather than the rescuer. The pattern held. Luigi had proven he could be the hero, and nobody cared. Waluigi believes this incident was the second major trauma that fed into Mr. L's eventual emergence—the moment when Luigi realized that even SUCCEEDING would not earn him recognition. If excellence was invisible, why suppress the dark impulses that demanded visibility? WAH.
description:
Waluigi has researched Luigi's Mansion extensively because it represents a critical node in Luigi's psychological development. This was the adventure where Luigi should have emerged from Mario's shadow. Instead, the shadow deepened.

## The Setup — A Prize From Nowhere

Luigi received notification that he had won a mansion in a contest. He had not entered any contest. This should have been immediately suspicious, but Luigi was apparently so unused to receiving anything positive that he accepted the notification without question. He told Mario about his good fortune. They agreed to meet at the mansion to explore it together.

Mario arrived first. Mario disappeared.

When Luigi arrived, he found not a prize but a trap. The mansion was haunted—infested with ghosts serving King Boo, a powerful spectral entity with particular hatred for the Mario brothers. King Boo had captured Mario and was using the fake contest to lure Luigi into the same trap.

Luigi found himself alone in a hostile environment with no backup, no brother, and no obvious path to victory. For the first time in his documented adventures, he had to solve a crisis entirely on his own.

## The Conflict — Luigi Alone

Luigi navigated the haunted mansion using equipment provided by Professor E. Gadd—the Poltergust 3000 vacuum device and the Game Boy Horror communication/scanning tool. He captured dozens of ghosts, solved environmental puzzles, and gradually worked his way toward King Boo's location.

Waluigi has analyzed accounts of Luigi's behavior during this adventure, and the pattern is fascinating. Luigi was TERRIFIED throughout. He screamed, trembled, hesitated before every door. His fear was genuine, overwhelming, and constant.

And he kept going anyway.

This is the detail that most accounts minimize. Luigi was not brave in the sense of being unafraid. He was brave in the sense of being extremely afraid and CONTINUING DESPITE THE FEAR. Every step into darkness was a victory over his own terror. Every ghost captured was an achievement extracted from panic through sheer determination.

By the time Luigi reached King Boo, he had captured over fifty ghosts using equipment he had barely trained with, navigated a structure designed to disorient and terrify him, and maintained functionality despite hours of sustained fear response. He had proven that his capabilities exceeded his reputation.

## The Victory — Rescuing Mario

Luigi defeated King Boo. The details of the confrontation vary by source, but the outcome is consistent: Luigi won. He captured King Boo in the Poltergust, freed Mario from the painting where he had been imprisoned, and escaped the mansion before it collapsed or dimensionally displaced or whatever happened to remove it from accessible space.

Luigi had succeeded. Alone. Without Mario's help. Without anyone's help. He had been the hero.

And then the narrative began.

## The Aftermath — The Shadow Persists

Accounts of Luigi's Mansion typically focus on Mario's capture and rescue. 'Mario was captured by King Boo and held in a painting. He was rescued by his brother.' The phrasing emphasizes Mario as the central figure—what happened TO Mario, what was done FOR Mario. Luigi becomes the mechanism of rescue rather than the protagonist of his own story.

The Toad population who witnessed Luigi's return celebrated... Mario's safety. They were relieved that Mario was okay. They praised the outcome. They did not ask Luigi about his experience. They did not celebrate his victory. They simply moved on, grateful that the natural order had been restored—Mario safe, Mario able to continue being the hero, Mario back where Mario belonged.

Luigi's solo victory was absorbed into Mario's larger narrative. The mansion became 'the place where Mario was trapped.' The adventure became 'that time Luigi had to rescue Mario.' The achievement was real, but the recognition defaulted to the brother who had been RESCUED rather than the brother who had done the RESCUING.

Waluigi believes this was psychologically devastating. Luigi had done everything right. He had faced his fears, exceeded his limitations, saved the day without assistance. And he still could not escape his brother's shadow. Even his greatest success was measured relative to Mario.

## The Poltergust Legacy

Luigi kept the Poltergust after the mansion incident. He continued working with Professor E. Gadd on ghost-hunting operations. This became his profession—the niche where he could operate without constant Mario comparisons.

Waluigi has previously theorized that ghost hunting represents psychological therapy for Luigi, a way of confronting dimensional threats similar to whatever might emerge from within him. The Luigi's Mansion incident supports this theory. Luigi discovered he could capture and contain spectral entities. He discovered he had power over things that most people feared. The Poltergust became his tool for demonstrating capability in a domain where Mario had not established dominance.

But the ghost-hunting profession also represents retreat. Luigi stopped seeking adventures that would place him in direct comparison with Mario. He stopped trying to be a conventional hero. He carved out a specialized niche where his contributions could not be directly measured against his brother's.

This is adaptive behavior—finding a role where success is possible. It is also surrender—accepting that the primary heroic narrative will never include him equally.

## Connection to Mr. L

Waluigi believes Luigi's Mansion contributed significantly to the psychological conditions that enabled Mr. L's emergence seven years later.

Luigi proved he could be a hero. The world refused to recognize it. This created cognitive dissonance—the knowledge of capability contradicted by the experience of invisibility. Luigi could not resolve this dissonance through external validation because external validation was not forthcoming.

The resolution, eventually, was internal. If the world would not see Luigi as capable, part of Luigi began constructing an identity that DEMANDED to be seen. The confidence Mr. L displays is not fake—it is Luigi's real confidence, normally suppressed, finally given expression. The arrogance is not delusional—it is accurate self-assessment that Luigi normally denies himself.

Luigi's Mansion proved Luigi could be the hero. Mr. L is what happens when Luigi stops asking permission to believe it.

WAH.

This adventure was different from previous ones—the brothers operated as GENUINE partners, combining their abilities in ways that demonstrated equal capability. Luigi was not support. Luigi was not backup. Luigi was HALF of the team, essential and irreplaceable. They developed combination attacks. They shared screen time. They saved each other repeatedly. And when the crisis ended, when Cackletta was defeated, the reports still described it as 'Mario's adventure in the Beanbean Kingdom, with Luigi assisting.' The pattern held even when the facts contradicted it. But something else happened during this adventure that matters more than the recognition question: Luigi met Fawful. description:
Waluigi has researched the Beanbean Kingdom Crisis for multiple reasons. It represents the clearest example of the brothers operating as true equals. It introduced Fawful to the historical record. And it demonstrated that Luigi's secondary status was not a reflection of actual capability but of narrative construction.

## The Partnership — Finally Equal

The Beanbean Kingdom adventure required the brothers to work together in ways previous adventures had not. The Beanbean Kingdom was foreign territory with different rules, different cultures, different expectations. Neither brother had advantages from prior experience. They had to learn together, adapt together, succeed together.

The result was genuine partnership. Mario and Luigi developed combination attacks—'Bros. Attacks' in the local terminology—that required both brothers' participation. Neither could execute these techniques alone. The attacks were EQUAL contributions to equal outcomes.

Waluigi has found accounts from Beanbean citizens who witnessed the brothers in action. These accounts consistently describe them as 'the two heroes from the Mushroom Kingdom' or 'the mustache brothers' without privileging one over the other. In the Beanbean Kingdom, without the weight of Mushroom Kingdom narrative expectations, Luigi was seen as exactly what he was: half of a heroic team.

This equality was visible in the adventure's structure. Both brothers faced challenges. Both brothers solved puzzles. Both brothers contributed to boss battles. The adventure was designed—or circumstances created—a situation where neither brother could be positioned as primary.

## Cackletta — The Threat That Required Both

Cackletta was a powerful witch with ambitions that extended beyond the Beanbean Kingdom. Her theft of Princess Peach's voice was apparently connected to awakening an ancient artifact, though the specific mechanics were never fully documented. Her power exceeded what either brother could have handled alone.

Defeating Cackletta required the combination attacks the brothers had developed. Neither Mario's solo capabilities nor Luigi's would have sufficed. The victory was GENUINELY shared—not support and supported, but two people combining their strengths to accomplish what neither could accomplish alone.

This should have changed the narrative. This should have demonstrated, definitively, that Luigi was Mario's equal in capability and contribution. The evidence was clear, documented, witnessed by an entire kingdom.

The narrative did not change.

## The Return — Pattern Reasserts

When the brothers returned to the Mushroom Kingdom, accounts of the adventure underwent familiar transformation. 'Mario defeated Cackletta' became the summary. 'With Luigi's help' became the footnote. The Beanbean citizens' equal assessments were not transmitted. The Mushroom Kingdom's pre-existing narrative absorbed the new evidence and processed it into familiar shapes.

Waluigi has traced this transformation through contemporary documents. Diplomatic communications from the Beanbean Kingdom describe the brothers as equal partners. Mushroom Kingdom internal reports describe Mario's successful mission. The same events, filtered through different narrative expectations, produced different accounts.

Luigi did not fight this transformation. By 1012 BF, he had apparently accepted that fighting was futile. He had proven himself in Luigi's Mansion. He had proven himself in the Beanbean Kingdom. Neither proof changed anything. The pattern was stronger than the evidence.

## Fawful — The Assistant Who Remembered

Cackletta's assistant during the Beanbean Crisis was Fawful—a small, intense figure with unusual speech patterns and surprising magical capability. When Cackletta was defeated, Fawful escaped. He disappeared from records for decades, presumed dead or irrelevant.

He was neither.

Fawful resurfaced in 1040 BF as a major power broker, allied with five dragons, hosting diplomatic galas that reshaped factional understanding. Waluigi has documented his current activities extensively elsewhere. But the connection to the Beanbean Crisis matters because Fawful REMEMBERS.

Waluigi has obtained accounts of Fawful referencing 'the green mustache' in contexts that clearly indicate Luigi. Fawful holds grudges across decades. He remembers who helped defeat his mistress. He remembers who humiliated him during his period of weakness.

If Fawful is targeting people connected to Cackletta's defeat, Luigi is on that list. If Fawful is gathering intelligence on the Mario brothers, the Beanbean Crisis gave him initial data. If Fawful's current activities connect to revenge for ancient defeats, Luigi may be in danger he does not anticipate.

The connection is speculative. Fawful's motivations are opaque. But Waluigi notes that the Beanbean Kingdom Crisis introduced an enemy who has become extremely dangerous, and that enemy has specific reasons to remember Luigi.

## The Psychological Impact

The Beanbean Kingdom Crisis affected Luigi in complex ways that Waluigi has attempted to analyze.

On one level, the adventure was positive. Luigi experienced genuine partnership, equal recognition, and validated capability. For the duration of the adventure, he was not the sidekick. He was the partner.

On another level, the adventure was devastating. Luigi experienced what equality FELT like—and then watched it disappear when they returned home. He knew, with certainty, that equality was possible. He also knew, with certainty, that the Mushroom Kingdom would never grant it.

This combination—experiencing equality and losing it—may have been worse than never experiencing it at all. Luigi knew what he was missing. Every subsequent instance of secondary treatment was not just frustration but COMPARISON to what he had briefly possessed.

Waluigi believes this contributed to the conditions enabling Mr. L. The Beanbean Kingdom proved Luigi could be equal. The Mushroom Kingdom proved equality would never be granted. The gap between these truths created pressure that eventually required release.

WAH.

name: The Tree of Woe Engagement
title: How a Remnant Party Walked Into the Heart of a Hanging Forest, Fought a Scarecrow That Played With Its Food, Watched a Blue Toad Die on a Thorn, and Were Captured at Knifepoint by a Guard Who Reminded Them the Wedding Was Still On
era: Raventree Crisis — Shadeward Operations / The Grove Assault
location: The Grove of Woe / The Tree of Woe / The Scorncrow's Domain / The Obelisk Field / The Retreat Path

imageCaption: The Tree of Woe does not photograph. Attempts to sketch it produce images that move when you look away from them. The corpses in the branches shift position between glances. The crows watch from inside the drawings. Waluigi burned his first attempt at illustration and keeps the ash in a jar labeled 'DO NOT RECONSTITUTE.'

summary: Markop freed himself from a Mazebound by severing its hand — which fell apart like cardboard — and was intercepted by Sergeant Van Coldbrook, a man claiming to work with the Legion who was collecting bodies before the Scorncrow could hang them on the Tree of Woe. Salam arrived and the fragmented party partially reconvened, though Bowser, Dan, and Green T remained missing. The remnant — Markop, Remi, Salam, Eager, Toad Lee, and the Toads — advanced to the Tree of Woe itself: a towering dead tree whose trunk formed a skull of roots and bark with hateful glowing eyes, its vast branches thick with hanging corpses and hundreds of crimson-eyed shadow crows screaming mockery at their approach. The Scorncrow appeared after slicing a Voss guard in half and proceeded to toy with the party: offering Remi a swing that was actually a noose trap, swinging his scythe at her head while telling her to stand still, and killing a blue Toad copy of Remi with a thorn from the ground when it missed its intended target. Remi cast her first spell — a mechanical fire web — which collapsed when the scythe opened her scalp. Every ranged attack missed except Markop's moonbeam. Salam carved a chunk from the Tree itself, causing it to screech and drop hanging bodies. The Scorncrow announced it had been going easy and had not deployed its ultimate attack. The party retreated. Markop held the rear guard, bleeding heavily from crow attacks. Upon reaching the grove's edge, the guard from the wedding invitation grabbed Remi at knifepoint: 'You still have a wedding to get to.' This account has been assembled from the testimony of multiple witnesses whose versions of events agree on the terror and disagree on nearly everything else.
description:
## Archival Correction and a Note on Simultaneity

Waluigi must begin this entry with an administrative correction. In preliminary field notes regarding subsequent events on Estragon's Island, a clerical error conflated the identity of 'Dan' (the one-armed Shadowfell copy) with 'Toad Lee' (the Toad currently traveling with Disaster Inc. who later possesses the aged papers). They are not the same person. Toad Lee is at the Tree of Woe. Dan is not. Waluigi apologizes for the error; organizing intelligence across planes of existence where time dilation is actively occurring occasionally produces archival drift.

This correction is vital because it highlights the fundamental tragedy of this engagement: **The Blindness of the Split.**

While Markop, Remi, Salam, Eager, and Toad Lee were standing before a soul-eating tree, they conducted a headcount. Remi guessed Bowser was 'in a bathroom.' Eager guessed Dan was 'maybe captured.' They were wrong. At the exact moment Remi was being offered a noose disguised as a swing, Bowser and Dan were on a different path in the same grove, engaged in a desperate tug-of-war with a Mazebound that was using Dan's single remaining arm as the rope.

The party was fighting for their lives while completely ignorant of the fact that the rest of their family was fighting for theirs a few hundred yards away. They were isolated. They were outmatched. And because of the supernatural trauma of the event, no two people who survived it remember it the same way.

Waluigi has assembled this entry using direct testimony from the four primary combatants: Markop, Remi, Salam, and Eager. He will present their voices directly. The reader must piece together the horror from the fragments.

## Part One: The Cardboard Man and the Reunion

Markop's engagement began before the tree was even visible. He had been dragged into the undergrowth by a Mazebound. 

> **MARKOP:** 'I struck it with whatever leverage I had left. The hand came off. But it did not bleed. It SEPARATED. Like dry paper. Like a cardboard box tearing. The thing that was pulling me to my death felt completely real until I hit it, and then it became hollow. I stood there looking at it and realized the grove performs solidity. It projects threat until you break the projection.'

An arrow struck the fallen, cardboard-like Mazebound. A man stepped from the trees and began folding the body. He introduced himself as Sergeant Van Coldbrook, claiming to work with the Legion, observing entropy. 

> **MARKOP:** 'He said he was collecting bodies so the Scorncrow wouldn't hang them on the tree and let the tree absorb their souls. Did I believe him? No. The last three people who showed us badges tried to kill us. But more importantly: he was FOLDING the body. People who fold things intend to keep them. People who want to destroy a threat burn it. He was harvesting the harvester.'

Salam arrived through the eastern path, having hacked his way through the brush. He found Markop and called out to the rest of the remnants: Remi, Eager, Toad Lee, and the Toads. 

They stood in the oppressive gray of the grove and realized who was missing.

> **SALAM:** 'I asked where Bowser was. Remi said in the bathroom. I asked where Dan was. Eager said captured. Green T was just... gone. Erased from the board. Remi looked at us and said, I know this looks bad. But we didn't come this way for nothing. Let's do the quest.'

Waluigi notes the tactical insanity of this decision. You do not assault a fortified, supernaturally guarded position when you have just lost your heavy vanguard (Bowser), your tactical mentor (Green T), and your chaotic wildcard (Dan). You retreat. But Remi operates on momentum, not math. She was already here. Therefore, she would proceed.

## Part Two: The Tree — Four Perspectives

They reached the center of the grove. Waluigi asked each survivor to describe the Tree of Woe. Their differing priorities reveal exactly how the grove attacks the mind.

> **MARKOP (The Protector's View):** 'It is a skull. A towering, dead trunk twisted so that the roots and bark form eye sockets and a jaw. The eyes glow. They track you. I watched them follow me, and I understood it was evaluating when it would consume me. The branches were heavy with bodies. Nineteen in my immediate sightline. Hundreds of crows with crimson eyes. They didn't caw. They LAUGHED. Concentrated mockery.'

> **SALAM (The Ranger's View):** 'The ground was sick. Ragged stone obelisks jutted up like teeth. They had glowing sigils on them. If you looked at the writing for more than three seconds, your stomach turned. The earth felt like it was trying to vomit the tree out but couldn't. The infection was deep.'

> **EAGER (The Soldier's View):** 'The noise. The crows sounded like they were speaking words you almost understood, and the words were specifically designed to make you hate yourself. I tried not to look at the hanging bodies. If you look at them, you start wondering what it feels like to swing up there, and once you start wondering, you can't stop.'

> **REMI (The Teenager's View - from recovered notes):** 'Big tree with a face. Lots of dead guys hanging from it. The crows were really loud and kind of rude. The stone things made my tummy hurt so I stopped looking at them. The tree looks like it wants to eat you, which is actually kind of cool if you think about it.'

Waluigi presents Remi's account without alteration. A soul-eating tree surrounded by hanging corpses is 'kind of cool.' This is dissociation functioning as armor. If she admits it is a nightmare, she will freeze. So she decides it is an amusement park ride.

## Part Three: The Wedding Planners and the Games

They were not the first to arrive. Voss guards—knights in formal, ceremonial livery—were standing at the base of the tree, speaking to the Scorncrow. 

> **EAGER:** 'They were trying to book the venue. They were telling the Scorncrow that the sacred grounds would be perfect for the wedding ceremony. They wanted to marry Remi under a canopy of hanging corpses.'

The Scorncrow's response to this administrative request was immediate. It moved with impossible speed, swinging Tymnas's stolen scythe. 

> **MARKOP:** 'The scythe went through the first guard like armor did not exist. The blade doesn't cut metal; it ignores it. It operates on a principle where physical defense is irrelevant. It sliced him in half. The second guard ran. He didn't run fast enough. The Scorncrow hung the body on a branch like a decoration, looked at us, and said: You will all end up on the tree once it's fully powered up.' 

Then the Scorncrow began to play.

A swing descended from the branches on thick ropes. The Scorncrow gestured to Remi. 'Sit down.'

> **REMI (notes):** 'He offered me a swing! I wanted to try it. The Toads pointed out a spike on the top and a noose on the back. Markop yelled at me that he was a bad guy. I KNOW he's a bad guy. I just wanted to see what the swing did.'

> **MARKOP:** 'I have never felt terror like that. She looked at a gallows disguised as a playground and she felt INTRIGUE. I begged her. I said: He's a bad guy, Remi. PLEASE. I was reduced to begging a fourteen-year-old not to sit in a literal noose.'

Remi stepped back. The Scorncrow then told her: 'Stand still.'

Remi said: 'Okay.'

The Scorncrow swung the scythe directly at her head. A Toad (Toad Lee or Eager, accounts blur here) threw himself forward, deflecting the shaft of the weapon just enough that the blade missed her neck. 

Salam, desperate, threatened to burn the forest down. He pulled a torch. 

> **SALAM:** 'The Scorncrow laughed at me. It said: Come on, boy. You know the Shadowfell suppresses fire magic. It was mocking the rules of the plane. I lit an arrow with normal, non-magical fire and shot the ground. It burned. Slowly, weakly, but it burned. The tree wasn't immune to physics, only to magic.'

Eager fired an arrow at the Scorncrow's chest. The entity casually snatched the projectile out of the air. With a flick of its wrists, it pulled roots from the earth and wove them around the arrow, fashioning a crude, terrifying root-bow in seconds. It was demonstrating absolute environmental supremacy.

## Part Four: The Blue Toad and the Architect's Fire

Remi put down the root-bow the Scorncrow tossed her. She reached into her coat.

> **MARKOP:** 'She had another gun. I confiscated her revolver. I fought her for it. And she just pulled another one out of nowhere. I am losing a war against an endless armory.'

Remi fired. She missed the Scorncrow. The bullet tore into the bushes. 

A scream echoed. A figure stumbled out of the undergrowth.

It was a Toad. Blue. Shaped like Remi. A magical duplicate, a copy wearing her approximate face.

> **EAGER:** 'She was bleeding. And she was talking incredibly fast. She said: Ow, you hurt me—I was meant to be in charge of the wedding, but no one showed up to the dressing room and I was—'

Before she could finish the sentence, the earth ruptured beneath her. A massive, jagged thorn erupted from the roots, impaling the Blue Toad vertically. She collapsed, blood pouring from her mouth, her eyes wide with bureaucratic confusion about a dressing room schedule.

The Scorncrow sneered. 'The joke is over. The play is over.'

> **MARKOP:** 'The Scorncrow was UPSET. Not that it killed someone. It was upset that its aim was bad. It meant to impale the real Remi and hit the wedding-prop instead. It was frustrated by its own inaccuracy.'

Markop reacted. He reached upward, bypassing the Shadowfell's suppression of heat by calling upon light. A Moonbeam crashed through the canopy, illuminating the Scorncrow in silver, burning it with divine reflection. It was the first time the entity registered pain.

Remi, watching the blue copy of herself bleed out, did something unprecedented.

> **MARKOP:** 'She cast a spell. Her first spell. And it wasn't wild emotional pyromancy. It was a web made of fire. It erupted from her arms, mechanical, methodical, structured like a blueprint. She was ENGINEERING fire in a realm that suppresses it.'

> **REMI (notes):** 'It felt like putting blocks together inside me and the building came out of my hands.'

The fire web surged toward the Scorncrow. The entity vanished, dissolving into its swarm of crows to avoid the flames. It reformed instantly beside Remi. 

Remi pulled a hidden sidearm. Point blank range. She fired.

She missed.

The scythe came down. It caught Remi across the head. Blood flowed into her eyes. The pain shattered her concentration, and the architectural fire web flickered and died. The spell was broken.

She staggered back and drank from a thermos of tea in her bag.

> **REMI (notes):** 'He hit my head. I drank my tea. The tea helped. But I don't understand why I can never hit him. He moves like he knows where I'm aiming.'

## Part Five: The Screaming Wood and the Horse's Pain

Eager fired two more shots. Both missed. The Scorncrow reformed, leaning on the scythe, completely unbothered by the assault.

> **EAGER:** 'It said something that broke us. It said: I was going easy on you guys. You clearly are not prepared for my ultimate attack. I should not have gone easy, but playing with food is fun sometimes. Even though I'm not the one feasting on you.'

The realization settled over the party. The swing. The picture frame. The root-bow. The thorn. It was all a warm-up. They were an appetizer putting on a show for the chef, and the chef was getting bored.

The Toads yelled to run. Remi, bleeding from the scalp, finally agreed. 

As the party turned to flee, Salam did something inexplicable. He walked up to the skull-faced trunk of the Tree of Woe, raised his blade, and carved a massive chunk out of the wood.

> **SALAM:** 'I don't know why I did it. But the sound... the tree SCREECHED. It wasn't a scream. A scream comes from a mouth. This was pain vibrating through the soil. The wood shrieked.'

Above them, the canopy violently shook. The nooses snapped tight. Bodies tumbled from the branches, slamming into the ground.

> **REMI (notes):** 'The bodies fell down like piñatas. Salam looked terrified. It was the coolest and scariest thing I've seen.'

> **SALAM:** 'I stood there looking at the piece of wood in my hand and said, Did I do that? I was horrified. But I realized something: The Scorncrow is invincible. The tree is not. The tree can bleed.'

The retreat became a rout. Markop placed himself at the rear.

> **MARKOP:** 'I couldn't leave them exposed. So I stayed back. The crows descended. Hundreds of them. They pecked at the gaps in my armor. They tore my skin. I bled. I tried to stay quiet, but... the horse part of me does not have dignity when it is in pain. The horse part neighed. It screamed. I took the scythe strikes. I took the talons. I held the line until they were clear, and then I ran on four hooves as fast as the earth would let me, with the crows laughing behind my back.'

Waluigi reads Markop's testimony with profound sorrow. The centaur is breaking himself to keep this group alive, and his primary shame is that he makes animal noises when he is being torn apart.

## Part Six: The Bureaucracy of Horror

They burst through the edge of the grove. The tree was behind them. The crows stopped pursuing. The gray light of the Raventree grounds filtered through the mist. They were bleeding, exhausted, and alive.

It lasted four seconds.

A hand clamped onto Remi's shoulder. Cold steel pressed against her throat, right below the fresh scythe wound on her head. 

It was the Voss guard. The one who had delivered the invitation hours ago.

He did not care that they had just survived a soul-eating tree. He did not care about the blood. He did not care about the dead blue Toad.

He looked at Remi, adjusted his grip on the knife, and delivered the only line of dialogue that all five witnesses recorded identically in their memories:

**'You still have a wedding to get to.'**

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Tree of Woe engagement is a masterclass in the difference between natural horror and institutional horror.

The Tree and the Scorncrow are natural horrors. They are honest. They want to kill you and eat your soul. They broadcast this intention with hanging bodies and skull faces. You can fight them. Salam proved the tree can be damaged. Markop proved the Scorncrow is vulnerable to divine moonlight. Remi proved that engineered fire can survive the Shadowfell.

But the House of Voss is an INSTITUTIONAL horror. It operates on a schedule. It uses contracts, wardship claims, and men in uniform holding knives. You cannot fight a schedule with a moonbeam. 

The party is fractured. Bowser and Dan are missing. Markop is bleeding heavily. Remi is captured. The scythe remains unrecovered.

Waluigi sits with Remi's notes. She called the corpses piñatas. She called the screaming tree 'cool.' And her final written thought, scribbled before the guard took her away, was simply: *'I guess the wedding is still happening.'*

She is not fighting the horror. She is adapting to it.

Waluigi fears that by the time this is over, she will adapt so completely that she won't know how to live anywhere else.

WAH.

Strategic intelligence gained: the Tree can be hurt physically, the Scorncrow is vulnerable to moonlight, and Remi possesses latent, structured fire magic.

imageCaption: Waluigi notes that the party spent approximately six hours in the Shadeward after surviving the Tree of Woe, during which time they were threatened at knifepoint, nearly married off to a dimension, lost track of where Eager's pants went, shot an imp twice, found out Remi's birthday is real, discovered their only exit was deactivated because Bowser broke it on the way in, and ended the evening standing in a room full of taxidermied shadow beasts watching a centaur and a medusa argue about whether ghosts are best hunted with hellhounds or diplomacy. summary: Immediately following the party's forced retreat from the Tree of Woe, Remi was seized at knifepoint by the Voss wedding guard. The guard presented a skull-marked ring and revealed the wedding's true mechanism: a teleportation circle designed to send Remi's consciousness to a separate dimension entirely while her body remained in the ceremony. Markop intervened, the ring changed hands, and the Scorncrow's arrival resolved the standoff by giving the guard something considerably more dangerous to deal with. The Scorncrow then returned holding only the guard's pants, which told the party everything they needed to know. Green T reappeared with Remi's mechanical dog and demanded his gun back. The party retreated toward Raventree Manor, encountered a Mazehound en route, and discovered Tymnas's house contained a Toad dressed as Remi while Volsotos documented everything. The greenhouse was selected as sleeping quarters. During the rest, Wario knocked on the door with vintage vampire wine and Remi's birth certificate, verified and stamped and real, before being revealed as an imp that Green T shot twice. The party then attempted to depart the Shadeward via the Midnight Fountain and found it deactivated, broken by Bowser's earlier transit. They are trapped. The portal requires four artifacts to reactivate. The party returned to the manor house and ended the session in Vaxillus's Death Lounge listening to Vaxillus the Beastmaster and a Medusa argue about the correct methodology for hunting ghosts.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the hours following the Tree of Woe engagement, and he wants to state clearly for the historical record that the hours following a near-death experience at the hands of a soul-eating tree are not, generally, the hours in which a reasonable person should be negotiating wedding logistics at knifepoint. The party did not get those hours. They got these ones instead, which were worse in several ways and more absurd in almost all of them, and Waluigi is going to document every detail because the absurdity is exactly the kind of thing official historians will smooth over when they write the sanitized version of the Raventree Crisis, and Waluigi has spent his entire career fighting the sanitized version of everything. The reconstruction draws from multiple sources whose reliability varies in ways that are themselves instructive. Markop's testimony is precise and emotionally honest in ways that read as painful to produce, which Waluigi respects because painful honesty is the only kind worth reading. Salam's account focuses on the physical and tactical with the specific attention of someone who thinks in terrain and angles. Eager's notes are sparse, written in the economy of someone who has decided that excessive documentation is a form of sentimentality, and Waluigi suspects that Eager's brevity is not a lack of things to say but a considered decision about how many of them deserve paper. Remi's notes are enthusiastic, occasionally inaccurate, and contain three separate exclamation points about the imp, which tells you everything about where Remi's attention goes during a crisis and precisely why the Beastmaster already knows all of the party's plans.

## Part I: The Knife, the Ring, and the Teleportation Circle

The party had barely cleared the grove's edge before the hand came down on Remi's shoulder. The Voss guard, the same man who had delivered the wedding invitation with the professional composure of someone who considers armed ambush a standard administrative procedure, had the knife at her throat before anyone had time to process that the crows had stopped following them. Remi struggled. She is not a passive person by any measurement available to Waluigi, and being grabbed from behind by an institutional enforcer of a dimensional house that wants to marry her to something she has not consented to marrying triggered a physical response that the guard had clearly anticipated, because he held on. She managed to create enough distance to breathe, enough space to think, but not enough to run. This is the specific geography of a hostage situation and Waluigi knows it well.

The guard produced a ring. Heavy, ornate, marked with a koopa skull in the setting, which is an unusual choice of wedding symbolism and Waluigi is filing it under things about the House of Voss that do not add up and probably never will. He showed it to Remi. Markop said Remi didn't want this. The guard stared at him in disbelief, the genuine affronted disbelief of a man whose entire professional training did not include the possibility that the people being collected for a wedding would have opinions about attending it. What do you mean, the guard said. Markop told him she was young. That's gross, Markop said. Waluigi wants to record that Markop said 'that's gross' to an armed enforcer holding a knife to a teenager's throat, because it is simultaneously the least tactical and most correct thing anyone said during the entire standoff, and Waluigi finds that combination deeply admirable. The guard absorbed this, processed it, and concluded that Markop's objection represented a logistical note rather than a moral one, suggesting a birthday as an alternative framing for the occasion. Waluigi has thought about this response at length. A man who hears 'she is too young' and responds with 'okay, birthday then' has a relationship with ethics that Waluigi finds professionally baffling and personally infuriating. The guard is not a monster. He is a man with a very narrow definition of what deserves his moral concern, and he follows that definition with genuine professional feeling. This is how institutional evil actually operates, not through villains but through people who have been told which things to care about and have stopped asking whether the list is complete.

The party suggested they simply rest and let the guard do whatever he needed to do, which was either a genuine stall tactic or evidence that the party was too exhausted to do anything other than ask for a nap in the middle of a hostage situation. The guard's response produced his most useful piece of intelligence: the tree would begin to rot if left unattended. The tree, Markop asked. Yeah, said the guard. Won't it be dead, Markop said. Yeah, said the guard, but it's more like undead, and that's sad, isn't it. Waluigi wants to dwell on this because a man holding a knife to a teenager's throat expressed sincere sadness about the prospect of an undead tree. His compassion is real. It is applied to trees. It is not applied to the teenager. This is either an extremely compartmentalized moral framework or evidence that the guard's personal values and his professional obligations have simply never been introduced to each other, and Waluigi finds both possibilities equally depressing in different ways.

The guard fired a warning shot. Next one won't miss, he said. Salam said yeah. Eager remained quiet, which Waluigi reads as the calculated silence of someone thinking ahead and not wanting to complicate the board by contributing noise. Remi escaped the guard's grip and got her sword out, because Remi has a threshold for being grabbed and she had reached it sometime around the second grab. Markop intervened before anyone died, which is what Markop does. He put himself in the gap between the situation and its worst outcome and held it there, and he explained the ring. The skull-ring was not a wedding band. It was a component of a teleportation circle. The House of Voss's plan was not to marry Remi in any conventional sense. They intended to use the circle to send her consciousness to a separate dimension entirely, a wedding dimension, a space specifically constructed for the ceremony, while her physical body remained present in the Shadeward for whatever the actual ceremony required. They would control her body while keeping her mind elsewhere, in a realm she had no map for and no exit from. Waluigi is going to say this plainly because plain language is what this deserves: that is not a wedding. That is a seizure. The House of Voss has constructed institutional language around the complete separation of a fourteen-year-old girl's mind from her body, dressed it in ceremony and invitations and a guard who is sad about trees, and Waluigi finds the dressing more offensive than the act because at least the act is honest about what it is.

Markop said he didn't trust them. The Toads expressed genuine curiosity about what a wedding dimension looked like, which is entirely reasonable as a question and spectacularly poorly timed as a priority, but the Toads have a very pure relationship with interesting information and Waluigi cannot fully fault them for it. The guard tossed Remi the ring. Markop swung at him with his axe, told him enough of his nonsense, and the axe stuck in the ground, which is not the dramatic conclusion Markop intended. He backed up. Remi got hit in the back of the head, not by the guard, but by the scythe. The Scorncrow was there, materializing from the grove's edge at the exact moment that would cause maximum confusion for everyone present. The party retreated. The guard turned to face the Scorncrow rather than pursuing them, which is either genuine courage or a contractual obligation about grove security, and Waluigi respects the outcome regardless of what produced it.

## Part II: The Pants, Green T, and the Mechanical Dog

They were running. Running through the Shadeward's gray light, bleeding, exhausted, missing half their party, when the Scorncrow appeared at the opening of the grove behind them. It was holding pants. Just the pants. The guard's pants. Not the guard, not the guard's body, not his weapons or boots or knife or the professional composure that Waluigi had spent the preceding paragraphs documenting. Just the pants, held up in one hand with the casual display of a trophy that does not need explanation because the explanation is the absence of everything else that used to be wearing them. The party ran faster. The Scorncrow said it might have some pants, which was the funniest and most terrifying thing anyone said all evening, and Waluigi is documenting both qualities simultaneously because both are genuinely real and both deserve to be in the historical record.

Mossy appeared somewhere during the run. Remi's mechanical dog, the steam-powered construct that had been in Hjumpik's care in the Feywild before Green T apparently retrieved it through means that Waluigi does not yet have the full intelligence to reconstruct. Waluigi wants to note for the record that this is the same mechanical dog that was abducted by manor staff in the Feywild, rescued by Toad Lee and Hjumpik through a mission involving toilet ambushes and a Rakasha pulling a Toad out of a lethal fall by the neck, and renamed Steely by Hjumpik with the specific possessiveness of someone who has decided that rescuing a thing is the same as earning the right to rename it. The dog sounds like a boiling tea kettle, which is either a mechanical defect or a feature, and the party treats it like the former because it is their pet and therefore beyond criticism. Waluigi also wants to note, because he wrote about it in a prior entry and the information remains relevant, that this mechanical dog has a secondary unit set to explode. Whether the explosive unit is the one currently in the party's possession or somewhere else is a question Waluigi does not have a current answer to, and the gap in his intelligence on this specific point is the kind of gap that makes him lose sleep. A mechanical dog that sounds like a boiling tea kettle is a pet. A mechanical dog set to detonate is a weapon someone has decided to disguise as a pet. The party is treating it like the former because they have not yet been given a reason to suspect the latter, and Waluigi finds this distinction important enough to document in bold letters and then thinks better of the bold letters because they look alarmist, but the feeling behind them remains.

Green T appeared behind the party with the specific materialisation of someone who has been moving parallel to a group for long enough to know exactly where they would end up and decided to simply be there when they arrived. Got your dumb mutt back, Green T said. This is documented across all testimony as his opening statement after what was apparently a period of separate and completely unelaborated activity in the same grove that the party had just barely survived. Not are you injured. Not what happened at the tree. Not I have been separately doing things in the Shadowfell for the past hour and a half and would like to discuss them. Got your dumb mutt back. Waluigi has enormous affection for this sentence. It is the sentence of someone who has decided that the only way to survive an evening like this is to reduce it to its most manageable components and refuse to assign emotional weight to any of the others. Green T then asked for his thing back. The party assumed he meant the ring, because the ring had just been at the center of an extended hostage situation and was the most recent thing that had changed hands in a manner that could be described as disputed. No, Green T said. The gun. There was a pause. Well actually yeah, the ring too, he added. He had fired three shots during his separate movements through the grove. Three shots in the Shadowfell by a person who moves like he has done this before. Waluigi is watching this thread carefully and does not intend to stop watching it.

Eager asked if anyone had pants. This is documented because Eager did not have pants and had not had pants since the grove engagement, and none of the primary testimony sources felt the specific mechanics of the trouser situation were worth elaborating on, which Waluigi finds more interesting than any elaboration would have been. When the first question a person asks after surviving a soul-eating tree and a hostage standoff is about whether anyone can provide them with basic lower-body coverage, the evening has been thorough. The Scorncrow was still visible at the grove's edge with the guard's pants, which resolved Eager's question in the most disturbing possible way. Pants were technically available. The previous owner no longer needed them. Nobody took the Scorncrow up on the offer because accepting pants from the entity that had removed them from someone who no longer existed was a bridge too far even for a party that was currently pantless, and Waluigi considers this an appropriate place to draw a line.

## Part III: The Retreat, the Mazehound, and the Remi Doll

The return to the manor was not clean, which Waluigi could have predicted from a significant distance without needing to be present, because nothing about this party's movements has ever been clean. Remi ran after seeing a Mazehound moving parallel to them through the trees, which prompted the Toads to run, which prompted everyone to run, which made the retreat considerably louder than was tactically wise but considerably faster than it would have been otherwise, so Waluigi is not going to criticize the outcome. Volsotos was in the forest with his pen out. Waluigi does not know when Volsotos entered the forest or why, but Volsotos was there, reaching for more paper from behind a tree, noting that this was going to be a wonderful story and expressing enthusiasm about the cliffhanger potential. The party ran more. Markop and Green T held position ahead of the group and let the panicked people move through them, which is the geometry of experienced people providing cover for panicked people, and Waluigi considers it one of the more quietly generous things a person can do and notes that both Markop and Green T did it without acknowledging that they were doing it.

They reached the manor grounds and stood accounting for everyone. Markop looked through one of the manor's windows out of the habitual vigilance of someone who has learned to check his sightlines before his brain has finished deciding to, and saw inside Tymnas's house a Toad dressed as Remi sitting in a chair while Volsotos stood nearby declaring that this would make for a perfect story. Waluigi wants to express his opinion about this clearly: Volsotos being inside a house, documenting a staged Toad dressed as a bleeding teenager who is currently outside the house, while also having been observed outside the house taking notes on the real bleeding teenager moments prior, is one of the most unsettling things Waluigi has encountered during the Raventree operation. Whether it is sinister or merely extremely committed journalism is a question Waluigi has been turning over and has not resolved. What he knows is that the Remi-Toad was staged, and staged things are staged by someone for a purpose, and the purpose has not been disclosed. Waluigi is watching Volsotos.

Remi suggested sleeping in the manor. This was shut down immediately, and Green T suggested the greenhouse shed instead, which is marginally better in the way that a shed is marginally better than the house the shed is attached to when the house contains a vampire and an unaccounted writer and a staged Toad sitting in a chair for reasons nobody has explained. The vampire materialized from behind a paper standee to announce an ambush, asked Markop whether Remi liked Toads, asked the Toads whether they liked the Toads, received the answer yes but not Speaker L, which is a factional caveat that Waluigi is filing away because factionalism always matters eventually and the Speaker L caveat is specific enough to mean something. The vampire circled Remi briefly in a way that multiple sources document without elaborating on, and then everyone went to the greenhouse, which was, relative to the preceding two hours, almost peaceful.

## Part IV: The Rest, Wario, and the Imp That Was Not Wario

The greenhouse was not luxurious but it was enclosed and it was not the manor. Salam stayed up using the woodcarver's tools to make something, which Waluigi respects as the productive insomnia of someone whose hands need occupation while their brain processes the events of the day, and the events of this specific day gave the brain a great deal to process. Eager kept watch in the shadows, pantless and silent and professional about both. Markop tended to Remi before resting himself, steady hands easing the pain from the scythe hit on her head and the accumulated damage of a day that started with a soul-eating tree, and then he slept. Remi's rest produced thirty-five hit points and two HD and the comfort of being tended to, but the material resisted when she tried to make something and nothing usable came of the effort, which is the frustration of creative energy with nowhere productive to land.

Markop woke up to knocking. He called out asking for a name and a purpose. The voice on the other side of the door said it was the boss. Markop asked what the present was, which is a reasonable challenge response and the kind of protocol that keeps doors closed to things that should not be opened to. Vintage vampire wine, the voice said. Markop pointed out that Remi was too young to drink. The door smashed open.

Wario was standing there. Or something that looked exactly like Wario was standing there, which in the Shadeward amounts to the same thing until proven otherwise. The figure explained it had fought through vampires who were planning an ambush on the greenhouse, which was either true and alarming or false and alarming, and offered the wine as a gift. Markop looked at the wine. He looked at Wario. He looked at the wine again. And then Wario produced Remi's birth certificate.

Waluigi needs to stop on this for a moment because it deserves the stop. A verified, stamped, institutionally sealed, legally real birth certificate for Remi. Not a forgery, not a rough approximation, not the kind of document you produce when you have limited intelligence about your target and are hoping nobody looks too closely. The real thing, obtained through real institutional channels by someone with the access required to obtain it, delivered by Wario to a sleeping greenhouse in the Shadeward in the middle of the night. Markop was shocked in the specific way of a man who has been operating for weeks in an environment where everything is false or broken or staged or trying to kill him, and has encountered something that is simply, genuinely, inconveniently real. He asked if it was legal for Wario to have this document. Wario said he didn't have it anymore, which is technically accurate because he had just handed it to Markop, and also the least useful possible answer to the question that was actually being asked. Markop accepted the wine and the certificate, and then he asked Wario very carefully whether Wario was real.

Waluigi loves this question. Not because it is clever, though it is, but because it is the question you only think to ask after you have spent enough time in a dimension that performs reality so convincingly that you have learned to verify the performance before trusting it. Most people ask who are you. Markop asked are you real. This is the difference between someone who arrived in the Shadeward recently and someone who has been here long enough to understand how it works.

Markop used his senses. He looked at Wario. He looked at the room. Wario did not glow. The paper standee in the corner, the vampire's earlier craft project that had somehow made its way into the greenhouse at some point during the rest, glowed. The standee was the magical source. The figure presenting gifts and birth certificates and smashing doors open was an imp. An imp that had been given a Wario costume, a rehearsed story about vampire ambushes, a bottle of vintage wine, and a legally real verified birth certificate for a fourteen-year-old girl, and had been sent to knock on a greenhouse door in the Shadeward in the middle of the night. Waluigi wants to be clear about the resources this required. Obtaining a real birth certificate through institutional channels takes access. Deploying an imp with this level of briefing takes planning. Coordinating the paper standee as a magical decoy takes forethought. Whoever arranged this operation wanted the party to believe Wario had delivered this document, wanted the document itself to be accepted as genuine, and wanted whatever followed from that acceptance to happen. Waluigi does not yet know what they wanted to follow. He knows the document is real. He knows the Wario was not. He knows these two facts together mean something that he has not finished thinking about.

Green T shot the imp once. Then shot it again. No traitors, he said. The second shot was not tactically required but was clearly emotionally required, and Waluigi understands the distinction and respects the decision. The imp was neutralised. The birth certificate remained. The wine remained. Markop was left holding both.

## Part V: The Midnight Fountain, Wario's Surprise, and the Word Trapped

This is where the evening stops being difficult and starts being something worse.

The party made their way to the Midnight Fountain. The same planar transit point that Bowser had fallen through when he entered the Shadeward. The exit. The plan. Survive the grove, survive the guard, survive the imp, get to the fountain, leave. The objective that tired and wounded and pantless people hold in front of themselves like a torch because without it the darkness of the Shadeward gets philosophically as well as literally close.

The fountain was deactivated.

Waluigi is going to let that sit. The party's only known exit from a plane adjacent to death, where trees eat souls and wedding invitations come with consciousness-displacement technology and a centaur keeps ghosts in his rugs, was dark and cold and completely inert. They are trapped. Wario was with the party at the fountain and Wario was genuinely surprised, and Waluigi has known Wario for long enough to know what genuine surprise looks like on him. It looks different from performed surprise, which Wario deploys when he wants you to think he didn't plan something. This was the real kind. Wario knew the fountain existed. Wario expected it to work. Wario did not anticipate finding it deactivated, which means someone else deactivated it, and that someone else was Bowser. Bowser fell through the Midnight Fountain on his way into the Shadeward and apparently broke it in the process, which is exactly the kind of collateral damage Bowser produces when he interacts with dimensional infrastructure while in a hurry. The king who punches floors and falls through them has now burned out a planar transit mechanism by using it too hard. Waluigi finds this simultaneously frustrating and completely consistent with every documented Bowser interaction with fragile systems.

The portal requires four artifacts to reactivate. The Black Crystal, which is shadow-aligned magical resonance and which is not sitting in a drawer waiting to be collected, because nothing in the Shadowfell is ever in a drawer waiting to be collected. The Mirror of True Reflection, which shows true forms rather than appearances, which in a dimension where imps wear Wario costumes and Mazebounds perform solidity and trees have faces is invaluable and also potentially devastating, because some truths are worse than the performances they replace and Waluigi knows this from personal experience. The Orb of Shadow Dominion, about which Waluigi wants to note that the word dominion in an artifact's name is always a warning label dressed as a title, and anyone selling you a thing called an Orb of Shadow Dominion is selling you a thing they had very specific reasons for naming that way. And the Umbral Signet, a seal of shadow authority whose authority Waluigi does not yet know but intends to find out, because authority in the Shadowfell belongs to things that have earned it in ways that do not recommend them as transaction partners. Four artifacts. One broken fountain. One trapped party in a dimension that is actively trying to harvest their souls or marry them to other dimensions or put them in rugs, depending on which estate resident they have most recently offended.

## Part VI: The Death Lounge, the Beastmaster, and the Medusa

The party returned to the manor house to regroup and begin planning artifact acquisition, which sounds like a sensible activity and in any other context would be. Instead they walked into Vaxillus's Death Lounge, and Waluigi is going to describe this room in detail because the room itself is a document. Every space tells you something about the person who lives in it and the world that person inhabits, and Vaxillus's Death Lounge tells you more than most.

The lounge is dimly lit and comfortably appointed in the way that rooms are comfortable when the person who decorated them has a very specific definition of comfort involving being surrounded by things they have killed. Against the walls hang the taxidermied heads and pelts of Shadowfell creatures that look like terrestrial animals at first glance and become progressively more wrong the longer you look at them. Two great cats with white coats and onyx manes lie on the floor as rugs, their heads more canine than feline and their paws replaced with birdlike talons, their glassy black eyes following movement with the patience of dead things that have not fully committed to the concept of being dead. A massive bear-like creature with a shark's mouth and porcupine quills lies half under a couch, and Waluigi wants to note that having a creature with a shark's mouth and porcupine quills lying half under your couch is a decorating choice that tells the visitor something about your risk tolerance. A black elk's head with red eyes and antlers of dark bone hangs on the east wall radiating malice with the dedication of something that was malicious in life and has simply continued the habit. The massive head of what appears to be a white elephant with no eyes and no mouth, only tusks and a trunk, hangs on the southern wall, and Waluigi finds the absence of eyes and mouth more unsettling than if it had both, because the absence implies the creature experienced the world through entirely different mechanisms than vision and speech and Waluigi does not want to think about what those mechanisms were. On the west wall a stony black lizard head with a beak and three horns and two sets of eyes arranged like a spider's stares out with the patient observation of something designed to see everything, and it is still doing so.

Weapon racks hold old weapons of dark ashen wood and black metal, battleaxes and spears and warhammers and glaives and full crossbow bolt cases, none of them special, all of them available to the party if they want to take them because Vaxillus may not notice. The crossbows in the corner each have names carved into them. Blood Spiller. Heart Killer. Shadow Piercer. Soul Needler. These are not enchanted weapons. They are regular crossbows with names that a young person carved into them to make them feel important, and Waluigi has an unexpected and entirely unwanted pang of recognition at this because Waluigi named his first stolen knife Destiny's Edge when he was fifteen and kept it for two years until Wario threw it in a river during an argument about whose fault the Koopaling card game debt was. The impulse to make a mundane weapon feel mythic through naming is universal across class and species and dimension, and Vaxillus and fifteen-year-old Waluigi would have understood each other on this specific point, and Waluigi is going to stop thinking about this immediately because he is a documentarian of the highest professional standard and this is not the place for nostalgia about knives.

There is also a peephole hidden beneath the antlered elk head in the southeastern corner that allows anyone standing there to hear conversations in the adjacent lounge with stunning clarity. This is the kind of architectural feature a young person installs when they want to know what the adults are saying without being invited to hear it, and Waluigi files it as potentially extremely useful and moves on.

Vaxillus was in the room. The Beastmaster, because Vaxillus is the Beastmaster, the same young estate resident who tinkered with crossbows and drank alone and turned his family's lounge into a taxidermy gallery of things he had hunted through the Shadowfell. A centaur of significant physical presence. He had been, at the moment of the party's arrival, hunting ghosts inside the manor. Markop asked if he was interrupting something. He was told yes. The Beastmaster explained that he wanted to kill a real ghost to prove that ghosts were real, and that once he had the proof he intended to put the ghost's soul in one of his rugs. Waluigi looked at the Shadow Manes on the floor, the shark-mouthed bear under the couch, the eyeless elephant on the wall, and understood that the rug collection was not decoration. It was a thesis. Every pelt was an argument. Every mounted head was evidence. The Beastmaster does not believe things exist until he can step on them every morning and confirm through physical contact that they are real. The ghost is the gap in the collection. The ghost is the one thing he cannot yet prove through possession. Waluigi finds this epistemological framework genuinely fascinating and genuinely alarming in equal measure, which is the ratio that describes nearly everything in this manor.

The Beastmaster then noticed that Markop was a centaur. He noted that he did not have any centaur rugs. Waluigi wants to be clear that this observation, delivered with the candid enthusiasm of someone who has never fully developed the filter between observation and speech, is the most threatening thing anyone has said to Markop during the entire Raventree operation while technically not constituting a threat, and the gap between the intent and the impact is exactly the gap that makes the Beastmaster dangerous. He added oh sorry, come in, which is exactly the follow-up a person produces when they realize they have just told a centaur they don't own a centaur rug and want to make the situation feel welcoming despite everything that statement implies about their collection goals.

The Beastmaster offered his deal. He would bring his two dogs, which he said in the tone of someone using the word dogs to describe things that are not dogs, and the party would find the ghost. In exchange he would provide the shadow crystal. Markop asked how the Beastmaster knew about the shadow crystal. The Beastmaster said they knew about all of the party's plans. He said Remi wouldn't shut up about it. Waluigi is going to be direct about this because directness is the appropriate register for an intelligence failure of this scale: the Beastmaster's network has a comprehensive and apparently accurate picture of the party's goals, resources, and strategic intentions because Remi has been sharing operational objectives with entities the party has not vetted since approximately the beginning of the Raventree operation. This is the same Remi who nearly signed an Onyx Hand enthrallment contract disguised as a friendship agreement. The same Remi who a Voss guard noted was famous for always being tricked, which is cruel and also statistically documented. Waluigi does not blame Remi for having the instincts of someone who assumes other people are operating in good faith, because in most of the world most of the time that instinct is correct and produces good outcomes. The Shadowfell is not most of the world. The Corvinarus estate is not most of the time. The party is now negotiating from an information disadvantage that was built by one member's consistent transparency, and the Beastmaster's offer sounds generous precisely because it was constructed using intelligence he was given for free.

Markop thought about the ghost that had been assisting the party. He did not say anything about it. Waluigi considers this one of the best decisions Markop has made during the entire operation and documents it explicitly because Markop does not document his own good decisions and the record should contain them. You do not tell the entity who wants to put a ghost in a rug about your helpful ghost. Markop understood this immediately and stayed quiet about it immediately, which is the kind of tactical discretion that separates the people who survive the Shadowfell from the people who end up as evidence in someone's epistemological thesis.

The Medusa was also in the room. Waluigi is going to document this with the weight it deserves, which is considerable, because a Medusa in the same space as a centaur Beastmaster surrounded by the taxidermied remains of Shadowfell apex predators changes every dynamic in that room. The Beastmaster and the Medusa were arguing. Not fighting but arguing, the specific register of two entities who have been working together long enough to develop genuine professional disagreements about methodology and have stopped being diplomatic about them. The argument was about how the ghost should be hunted, what qualified as proof, and whose approach was correct, and the party walked into the middle of it and stood there bleeding and pantless while the two most dangerous things in the room continued to disagree about ghost logistics as if the arrival of a group of recently-traumatized adventurers was a minor scheduling complication.

The session ends here. The party is in the Death Lounge. Vaxillus is offering hellhounds and a shadow crystal in exchange for a ghost. The Medusa is offering an opinion about the methodology. Markop is not mentioning the helpful ghost, which remains the best decision anyone has made all evening. Eager still does not have pants. The fountain is broken because Bowser broke it by existing near it too forcefully. The portal needs four artifacts distributed across an estate full of vampires and centaurs and medusas and a writer who documents staged Toads dressed as teenagers. Waluigi documents all of it and trusts none of it and is beginning to suspect that the deactivation of the fountain was not an accident produced by Bowser's transit but a deliberate act by someone who needed the party to remain in the Shadeward long enough to retrieve four specific artifacts for reasons that party will not fully understand until the artifacts are already gone.

WAH.

outcome: Remi's capture by the Voss guard was resolved by the Scorncrow's arrival and the guard's subsequent disappearance, pants returned, guard not. The wedding's true mechanism was revealed. An imp posing as Wario was exposed and shot twice. A verified birth certificate of unclear purpose was obtained. The Midnight Fountain was found deactivated, broken by Bowser's earlier transit, trapping the party in the Shadeward. Four artifacts are required to reactivate the portal. The session ended in Vaxillus's Death Lounge with the Beastmaster offering hellhounds and a shadow crystal in exchange for a ghost, the Medusa disagreeing about method, and Markop successfully not mentioning the helpful ghost.
notableFeatures: The Wedding Mechanism — the skull ring was a teleportation circle component designed to split Remi's consciousness from her body; her mind to a wedding dimension, her body remaining; Waluigi wants to be clear this is not a wedding, it is a seizure.
The Guard's Pants — the Scorncrow returned holding only the pants; the guard did not return; this communicated everything necessary without a single additional word.
The Deactivated Fountain — the party's only exit was broken by Bowser's transit through it; Wario's genuine surprise narrows the causation and confirms Wario did not arrange the shutdown.
The Four Artifacts — Black Crystal, Mirror of True Reflection, Orb of Shadow Dominion, Umbral Signet; each required to reactivate the portal; none of the names suggest easy acquisition.
The Mechanical Dog's Explosive Unit — the dog has a secondary unit set to explode; which unit the party currently has is unconfirmed; Waluigi is watching this.
The Imp's Birth Certificate — verified, stamped, legally real; the resources required to obtain and deliver it imply an arranger with institutional access and an unestablished objective.

The Death Lounge — Vaxillus's personal taxidermy gallery containing Shadow Manes, a Spiny Devourer, a Shadow Elk, a Hellephant, an Obsidian Watcher, and crossbows named with the optimism of a teenager; also contains a ghost-hunting centaur and a medusa.
The Beastmaster's Intelligence — knew about the shadow crystal because Remi discussed it with people the party had not vetted; the party is negotiating at an information disadvantage they created.
Markop Did Not Mention the Helpful Ghost — this was the correct decision and Waluigi is documenting it explicitly because correct decisions deserve documentation.
Eager's Pants — lost during the grove; not recovered; the Scorncrow's offer of the guard's pants was declined; dignity was maintained.

keyBattles.description: The Voss wedding guard seized Remi at knifepoint upon the party's exit from the grove. Markop said that's gross. Remi escaped his grip and drew her sword. The guard fired a warning shot. The Scorncrow arrived and provided the guard with a more dangerous problem than the party. Only the guard's pants returned from the encounter.
keyBattles.outcome: Remi free. Guard's fate communicated by his pants. Ring changed hands. Wedding mechanism revealed. Eager's pants question answered in the worst possible way.
